title: Harvard plates show that the 1937 occultation of ASASSN-24fw had the same ingress shape and duration (within 4 days) as the 2024-2025 event; the period is 15,998.3 days
abstract: Question: are the 1937 and 1981 Harvard-plate events of the 4-mag occultation star ASASSN-24fw real, and did the occulter keep its shape over two 43.8-year orbits? Earlier papers called the plate events possible and said the plates cannot compare event shapes. Method: DASCH DR7 data (3,212 plates, 1889-1989) with 40 same-brightness control stars on the same plates, a likelihood that includes plate limits, and a template of the 2024-2025 event from ZTF, ASAS-SN and one published egress point. Results: the star is absent on 8 of 8 informative nights in 1937 and 6 of 6 in 1981 while 88-100% of controls are visible (quiet-record rate 3.1%; p = 8e-13 and 8e-10). The 1937 ingress has the same slow-then-fast shape as in 2024 (time-stretch factor 1.0-1.15, 68% range 0.74-1.76). The 1937 event lasted 251 +- 4 d between the 0.87-mag crossings, against 247-248 d in 2024-2025; at 95% it was at most 4.3 d shorter. The ingress times give P = 15,998.25 (+0.25/-0.87) d, and a scan of 20-100 yr with all plate and survey data gives one solution (15,998.35 d; no-repeat model worse by 80.9 in ln L). Free dust on orbits around the star would shear; the stable duration requires a semi-major-axis spread below 0.0013 au, so the occulter is probably bound to a companion or held by the binary. Next ingress: 2068 July 9 (near solar conjunction); egress 2069 March 14. Limitations: the modern egress shape is assumed from one published point; the 1937 times rest on 7 plate detections.

display.caption: The 2024-2025, 1937 and 1980-1981 occultations of ASASSN-24fw on one time axis (P = 15,997.5 d). Blue: detections; orange triangles: plate non-detections (star fainter); gray: 2024-2025 template.
Ingress and egress aligned at the 0.87-mag crossing: the 1937 Harvard plates follow the 2024 ZTF and ASAS-SN ingress.
Top: full 1889-2025 record with event windows for P = 15,998.3 d and the next event in 2068-2069. Bottom: log-likelihood of all data against trial period (20-100 yr).

citations.reason: Zakamska et al.: circumsecondary-disc occultation, P = 15,999 +- 2 d. We confirm P with higher precision but find the 1937 deep plate limits are real, and we measure the event shapes that they said the plates cannot compare.
Fores-Toribio et al.: 2024-2025 light curve, durations and the Perkins V egress point that we use as the modern egress anchor; we confirm the 43.8-yr period that they called likely.
Shah et al.: ring model around a substellar companion.
Nair & Denisenko: first report of the 1937 and 1981 plate events and the 43.8-yr period.
